sections.h2: What does Idaho landlord tenant law cover when you sell a rental?
sections.html:
Idaho's rules for rentals are short and mostly sit in two places: the unlawful detainer chapter of Idaho Code title 6 and the tenancy provisions of title 55. They set deposit refunds, written notices, eviction steps and what a tenant can do when a landlord fails on repairs. A seller who owns a tenant-occupied house needs to know which of those rules carry over to the buyer.

The short version is that a sale does not erase the tenant's rights. Under Idaho Code 6-321(3), if a rental changes ownership during a tenancy, the new owner is liable for refund of the security deposits. The unlawful detainer statute also speaks of the landlord's "successor in estate," which shows the law expects ownership to change hands during a lease.

sections.h2: How do security deposits work in Idaho, and who owes them after a sale?
sections.html:
Any amount a tenant deposits with the landlord for a purpose other than rent counts as a security deposit. When the lease ends and the tenant surrenders the premises, the landlord must refund everything except amounts needed to cover the contingencies named in the deposit arrangement. Idaho Code 6-321 forbids keeping any part of the deposit for normal wear and tear.

The statute defines normal wear and tear as deterioration from the use the unit is meant for, without negligence, carelessness, accident, misuse or abuse by the tenant, the household, or their guests.

  • Refund within 21 days if the agreement sets no time, and always within 30 days after surrender.
  • If you refund less than the full amount, include a signed statement itemizing what was kept, why, and a detailed list of expenditures from the deposit.
  • If a third-party manager handles the property, the deposit must sit in a separate account at a federally insured institution, apart from the manager's operating account. The rule does not apply to owners, certain affiliated managers, real estate licensees or qualifying nonprofits.

When you sell, make sure the deposit amounts and lease dates in your records match the tenant's. Because the buyer takes on the refund duty, ask your closing agent how the deposit will be handled and get it in writing.

sections.h2: What notices can an Idaho landlord give a tenant?
sections.html:
Idaho Code 6-303 lists the situations in which a tenant becomes guilty of unlawful detainer. A tenant is in unlawful detainer if they stay after the lease term ends without permission, or after a default in rent and a three day written notice, or after failing another lease condition and a three day notice.

The rent notice must demand payment of the stated amount due or possession of the property. It must also tell the tenant that if a court enters judgment, a residential tenant will have 72 hours to remove belongings. The notice may be served at any time within one year after the rent becomes due.

  • Nonpayment. Three days' written notice demanding the stated rent or possession.
  • Other lease violations. Three days' written notice requiring performance or possession. Within three days, the tenant or an interested person can cure the problem or pay and save the lease from forfeiture, unless the violation cannot be performed afterward.
  • Assigning, subletting or waste. A tenant who does this contrary to the lease ends the lease, and the landlord can serve a three day notice to quit.
  • Controlled substances. Unlawful delivery, production or use on the leased premises during the term is also a ground under the statute.

A tenant on farmland who holds over more than 60 days after the term with no demand or notice to quit is deemed to hold by permission for another full year.

sections.h2: How can a month to month tenancy end before a sale?
sections.html:
A tenancy at will, however created, ends when either side gives written notice of not less than one month. Idaho Code 55-208 says the landlord gives notice in writing to remove from the premises within a period of not less than one month, specified in the notice. The tenant ends the tenancy by written notice that it will vacate on a stated date, also not less than one month out.

The unlawful detainer statute links to this rule. For a tenancy at will, the landlord must first end it by notice, as the civil code prescribes, before the tenant is in unlawful detainer for staying.

If you want the house vacant at closing, start the written notice early and keep a copy. Plan on at least a month from the notice date before the tenant can be required to leave under a tenancy at will.

sections.h2: How does an eviction case end, and what do tenants get to remove?
sections.html:
After a court finds for the landlord, the tenant has a short window to take belongings, then the sheriff restores possession. Under Idaho Code 6-316(2), a residential tenant has 72 hours to remove belongings, while a commercial tenant or a tenant with a tract of five acres or more has seven days. A court may grant a commercial tenant longer on a finding of good cause.

The landlord or the landlord's agent may deliver a writ of restitution, or give the sheriff a copy and ask the sheriff to deliver it. After the removal period and three days after the court's finding, the sheriff restores possession by removing the tenant. The landlord may then remove and dispose of remaining property, subject to any security interests, without further compensation to the tenant.

The court can also award the landlord reasonable costs for removing property and restoring the premises when good cause is shown. For a seller, the practical lesson is that eviction is a court process with fixed steps. The statute routes removal through the sheriff and the court.

sections.h2: What can a tenant do if the landlord does not make repairs?
sections.html:
A tenant can sue for damages and specific performance, but must first give three days' written notice listing each failure. Idaho Code 6-320 allows the action for failure to provide reasonable waterproofing and weather protection, failure to maintain landlord-supplied electrical, plumbing, heating, ventilating, cooling or sanitary facilities, hazardous conditions, failure to return a deposit when required, breach of a lease term materially affecting health and safety, and failure to install approved smoke detectors.

If the landlord does not perform or cure within three days after service, the tenant may file. In an action solely for specific performance, the court must set trial within 12 days of the complaint, and service must come at least five days before trial. If the tenant also seeks damages, that fast schedule does not apply.

Smoke detectors get their own process. The landlord must verify at the start of the rental that working detectors are installed. If the landlord fails, the tenant can send written notice by certified mail, and if detectors are not installed within 72 hours of receipt, the tenant may install them and deduct the cost from the next month's rent. The section does not apply to tracts of five acres or more used for agricultural purposes.

Before you sell a tenant-occupied house, fix or document any open repair items.

sections.h2: What should you do before selling a house with tenants in Idaho?
sections.html:
Gather the lease and deposit records first, then decide whether the tenant stays or leaves.

  1. Locate the signed lease, any addenda, and proof of the deposit amount and where it is held.
  2. Check whether rent is current and whether any notice has already been served.
  3. Decide whether the tenant will stay under the existing lease or whether you will give written notice for a tenancy at will.
  4. Tell the closing agent how the deposit will transfer to the buyer.

Our Idaho squatters rights and adverse possession guide covers people who stay without a lease. For lease questions, the Idaho Court Assistance Office offers self-help information at courtselfhelp.idaho.gov.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work with a tenant in the house?
sections.html:
We can buy a house with tenants in it, as it stands. We review the lease, the deposit and the condition of the property before making any offer, and we do not quote a price here. The existing tenancy goes with the sale, so the deposit refund duty passes to the new owner under 6-321(3).

A cash purchase does not skip the legal steps for ending a tenancy. If you want the tenant out, the notices and court steps above still apply. This page is general information, not legal advice, so confirm details with the court, the county sheriff or an Idaho attorney.

faqs.q: How long does an Idaho landlord have to return a security deposit?
faqs.a: Within 21 days if the agreement fixes no time, and in any event within 30 days after the tenant surrenders the premises. A partial refund needs a signed itemized statement.

faqs.q: Who owes the tenant's deposit when a rental house is sold?
faqs.a: The new owner. Idaho Code 6-321(3) says that if the property changes ownership during a tenancy, the new owner is liable for refund of the deposits.

faqs.q: How much notice must a landlord give for unpaid rent?
faqs.a: Three days' written notice stating the amount due and demanding payment or possession. The notice must also warn that a residential tenant has 72 hours after a judgment to remove belongings.

faqs.q: How much notice ends a month to month tenancy in Idaho?
faqs.a: At least one month in writing, from either the landlord or the tenant, under Idaho Code 55-208. The notice must specify the date.

faqs.q: How long does a tenant have to move out after an eviction judgment?
faqs.a: A residential tenant has 72 hours to remove belongings. A commercial tenant or a tenant on five acres or more has seven days, and a court may allow a commercial tenant longer for good cause.

faqs.q: Can a landlord keep a deposit for normal wear and tear?
faqs.a: No. Idaho Code 6-321(1) says the landlord shall not retain any part of the deposit to cover normal wear and tear.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house that has tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. The sale does not end the tenancy, and the new owner takes over the deposit refund duty. A cash buyer can purchase a rented house as it stands, after reviewing the lease and condition.
